issue.title: Sync #2270: exec-server tests follow main's one-way credential broker; relay noise flake fixed

repository.name: CorbanuTerminal
repository.description: Corbanu Terminal: a capital-markets-focused AI coding and agent terminal.

issue.body:
Fixes the exec-server rows of #2270 on the sync branch (#1532), except the five `shell_snapshot_v2` rows, which sec-2347 (#2355) is handling.

Rerun on current sync (4ecfd4990f, glitch, Rust 1.99.1): the lib had 450 passed and 4 failed (the 3 masking rows plus the relay noise flake), and `exec_process` had 56 passed and 5 failed (the 5 `shell_snapshot_v2` rows).

**1. `native_request_handles_remote_proxy_config_for_platform` × 3 (test aligned to main's policy; no production change).**
The test expected upstream's fail-open: when a child's shell startup is one upstream's engine can't mask (`BASH_ENV`, `SSH_CLIENT`, an extra login option), the child gets the real `OPENAI_API_KEY`. On Corbanu, every proxy uses main's hardened engine (D353, applied in #1724). Upstream's engine and its snapshot restore stay off (D354), and brokering is one-way (#436). So the child gets a `sk-proj-…` placeholder, and upstream's `restore_and_disable_brokered_credentials` call does nothing there.
- The test now asserts that the real key never reaches the child when brokering is on (Linux/macOS).
- It still asserts that the key is unchanged when brokering is off, and on Windows, where unsandboxed native launches drop the proxy entirely.
- Masking is not weakened anywhere.

Note for reviewers: the `tracing::warn!` in `process_sandbox.rs` says "running with unmasked credentials". That wording is upstream's. On Corbanu the credentials stay masked, so it is now inaccurate. I left the production code untouched.

**2. `relay::noise_tests::malformed_handshakes_preserve_active_streams_and_admission_recovers` (timing flake; test-only fix).**
- Alone it passed 30/30 and the relay module 5/5; in full-lib runs it failed 1 of 9 (it lost diagnostic spans at line 808; #2270 saw lost events at line 837).
- Cause: tracing-core caches each callsite's interest process-wide. This is the race #1413 fixed with `ScopedTestSubscriber`. If the test's `with_subscriber` dispatcher was the only live one when it registered, `has_just_one` let a concurrent test thread with no subscriber cache `Interest::never` for the shared Noise diagnostic callsites.
- The fix registers an inert second dispatcher first and rebuilds the interest cache once the test's dispatcher exists. Afterwards, the Mac full lib passed 10/10 (458 tests).

**3. `exec_process_signal_interrupts_process::{local,remote}`: environment, not code.**
These pass when the test runs in the foreground (glitch run above). They fail with "deadline has elapsed" only when the test binary inherits SIGINT as ignored, for example when started with `nohup cmd &` from a non-interactive shell, as the #2270 run was.
- Reproduced on glitch: `(trap '' INT; exec <exec_process bin> exec_process_signal_interrupts_process)` fails both rows.
- Pipe-mode children keep `SIG_IGN`, and POSIX `sh` cannot trap a signal that was ignored on entry.
- Main behaves the same way: only PTY children reset signals. No test change. Whether pipe children should reset SIGINT/SIGQUIT is a product question in `utils/pty`, which I'll file separately.

**4. `shell_snapshot_v2` × 5:** untouched (sec-2347, #2355). I'll rerun them after it merges.

Also adds a ledger row in `ledger-rust-v0.167.0-compile.tsv`.

Gates so far: `cargo clippy -p codex-exec-server --tests -D warnings` (1.99.1) is clean, `cargo fmt --check` is clean, and the Mac lib run is 458/458.

issue.title: fix(security, sync): filter credential copies from exec-server's in-memory shell snapshot (#2356) — needs security sign-off

repository.name: CorbanuTerminal
repository.description: Corbanu Terminal: a capital-markets-focused AI coding and agent terminal.

issue.body:
Fixes #2356. Part of #2270 (the five `shell_snapshot_v2` rows).

## What
Upstream's executor-side shell snapshot (`shell_snapshot_v2`, off by default) replayed startup-file exports from executor memory without Corbanu's #310 secret-name list or #2314's credential-value filter. This applies main's owner-approved rule (#2332; sync port for core's file snapshot is #2355) to exec-server:

- **Value section** (`exec-server/src/shell_snapshot_filter.rs`): after startup, the capture also lists every shell variable's raw value, exported or not (bash/zsh/sh), framed `#values … #end <count>` and validated; a missing, empty or torn section fails the capture. The exported environment is a second source for the filter.
- **Filter**: a capture-local `OutputGate` (plus the process gate when armed) holds #310 secret-named values, core's `disclosure_gate::env_values` credential rules (mirrored here; core-only), and credential-looking values of plain-name policy excludes (#310 provider names reach the executor as excludes). An export whose value carries one, or whose name is #310 secret-named, is not replayed; a function or alias that still contains one refuses the snapshot (normal startup). So `GH_TOKEN=…; export HIDDEN_HEADER="Bearer $GH_TOKEN"` is never replayed, even when `GH_TOKEN` is unexported.
- **Broker path** (credential masking on, zsh): exports belong to the broker, so only functions, aliases and the final replay script are checked (placeholders restored first). Omitting exports there should follow the owner's broker-path decision for core (#2355 / D640) — follow-up noted below.
- **Bash replay runs `bash --norc -pc`**: bash sources `~/.bashrc` for `bash -c` when stdin is a socket (as under the Linux sandbox) or `SSH_CLIENT` is set, even in privileged mode. Replay therefore re-ran startup, reintroducing exports the snapshot filtered (fail-before: `bash_replay_never_reruns_startup_files` replays `HIDDEN_HEADER=Bearer ghp_…` without `--norc`) and calling user-shadowed builtins. This was the real cause of the Linux failures `filters_profile_exports_and_stays_in_memory::remote_sandbox` (exit 41) and `capture_failure_falls_back_and_retries::remote_{pipe,tty}_recovery` (`xxxx`).
- zsh's value capture runs under `emulate zsh` (an argv[0] starting with `c` selects csh emulation).
- The six `credential_masking=true` rows of `shell_snapshot_v2_remote_managed_proxy_uses_prepared_execution_context` are ignored with an S3b reason: they assert upstream's credential engine (startup files see the real key; inherited `AUTH_ALIAS` rewriting; configured providers), which Corbanu keeps off (D353/D354). `masked_bash`/`bash_profile_fallback` stop at `exit 42` (`AUTH_ALIAS` is not rewritten), the zsh rows at `exit 48` (startup sees a placeholder); the two fallback rows also assert #2365's warning.

## Evidence
- macOS (Rust 1.99.1, at f426ec07e5): `codex-exec-server` lib 480/480; `exec_process` 66 passed / 1 failed / 17 ignored — the failure is #2143 (`codex_home_symlink_opt_out…`, same on base). Base had 6 failing `shell_snapshot_v2` rows.
- glitch Linux (Rust 1.99.1, at 19815fd306; the last commit only changes the broker path, which needs zsh, absent there): lib 475/475, `exec_process` 55 passed / 0 failed / 17 ignored (base: 56 / 5 failed / 11 ignored).
- Fail-before: the 8 real-shell filter tests (bash/sh/zsh copies; function/alias refusal) all fail with the filter disabled; the `--norc` test fails without `--norc`.
- clippy (1.99.1) clean on `codex-exec-server --tests`.

Base failures of the six ignored rows: on macOS at b09fb8bf49 all six fail (masked_bash and bash_profile_fallback exit 42; zsh_profile_gateway_fallback, masked_zsh_inherited_credentials, zsh_unsupported_profile_fallback exit 48; masked_zsh_profile_credentials exit 50 with the #2365 warning); on Linux the two bash rows fail the same way (#2270), the zsh rows skip (no /bin/zsh). Ignoring them leaves the broker path (masking on, zsh) without an end-to-end test on this branch.

## Needs security sign-off (two choices main has no rule for)
1. **Which policy excludes count as #310 provider credentials.** Main registers the values of #310's removed provider names unconditionally. The executor only receives them mixed into `env_policy.exclude` with runtime excludes (e.g. a `1` flag) and user excludes, so this PR registers a plain-name exclude's value only when it looks like a credential (main's `is_plausible_secret`: 8+ bytes, 16+ or two character classes, not an existing path). Names that look like credentials (`*KEY*`, `*TOKEN*`, …) are covered by main's env rules anyway, so the gap is a short, low-variety provider value under an unusual name.
   - (a) As implemented. **Recommended**: the gap is narrow and the alternative refuses or degrades snapshots for ordinary excludes.
   - (b) Register every plain-name exclude value of 3+ bytes (closest to main). A short runtime or user-excluded value (`denied`, a version string) would then drop unrelated exports and refuse snapshots whose functions mention it.
   - (c) Add a protocol field so core sends #310's provider names separately (exact parity; touches core and the exec-server protocol).
2. **Broker path exports.** With credential masking on (zsh), this PR checks functions, aliases and the replay script but leaves exports to the broker; omitting #310 names there would unset brokered placeholders. Recommended: follow whatever the owner picks for core's broker path on #2355, as a follow-up here. Refusals on that path use upstream's fallback, whose warning is #2365.

issue.title: fix(sandbox, sync): spelling-independent Seatbelt carve-out order + exec-server symlinked-root test (#2143)

repository.name: CorbanuTerminal
repository.description: Corbanu Terminal: a capital-markets-focused AI coding and agent terminal.

issue.body:
Fixes the macOS-runner-only items of #2143 on the sync branch. Related: #2051 (exec-server list).

## Cause (seatbelt ordering)
The runner's `TMPDIR` is `/var/folders/...`; the tests' cwd is spelled `/var/...` while the writable root resolves to `/private/var/...`. In `get_writable_roots_with_cwd_impl` (`protocol/src/permissions.rs`) a default carve-out (`<cwd>/.codex`, protected even when missing) is dropped when an explicit entry for the same path exists, but that check compares spellings, so on the runner the default stayed first and the explicit `.git/.agents/.codex/.aws` entries were appended after it: `.codex, .git, .agents, .aws` instead of `.git, .agents, .codex, .aws`. Local Macs passed only because workers' `TMPDIR` is a canonical path. Reproduced locally with `TMPDIR=$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)`: both tests fail on the sync base, pass with this PR.

## Change
- **protocol**: the explicit carve-outs are computed first; a default carve-out that one of them also produces is skipped and appears at the explicit entry's place. The **set** of carve-outs is unchanged (before: `dedup(defaults ∪ explicit)`, after: `dedup((defaults \ explicit) ∪ explicit)`); only the order of a duplicate changes, and only when the cwd's spelling differs from the root's (with a canonical cwd the old spelling check already removed the same duplicates). No exclusion is dropped. New macOS test `writable_root_carveouts_do_not_depend_on_the_cwd_spelling` (cwd under `/tmp`): fails on the base (`.codex` first), passes here.
- **exec-server test**: `codex_home_symlink_opt_out_respects_host_config_and_scope` asserted upstream's refusal of symlinked writable roots and its `allow_symlinked_codex_home` opt-out. Corbanu does not take that refusal (S3a ledger row for `sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs`: a symlinked writable root is granted at its real location), as `exec/tests/suite/seatbelt.rs` already asserts. The test (renamed `codex_home_symlink_roots_write_at_their_real_location`) now asserts every root writes and the write lands in the link's target. Test-only; it failed locally on every Mac, not only on the runner.

## Evidence
- macOS (Rust 1.99.1, runner-like `TMPDIR=/var/folders/...` and the default TMPDIR): `codex-protocol` lib 450/450, `codex-sandboxing` lib 173 passed / 3 ignored (base: the 2 seatbelt tests fail with `/var` TMPDIR).
- macOS `codex-exec-server` (`--no-fail-fast`): lib 458/458; `exec_process` 67 passed / 6 failed / 11 ignored; all other 21 test binaries pass. The 6 failures are the `shell_snapshot_v2_remote_managed_proxy_uses_prepared_execution_context::*` rows owned by #2270/#2356 (PR #2369, waiting for security sign-off); unchanged by this PR.
- clippy `-D warnings --all-targets` (1.99.1) clean on codex-protocol, codex-exec-server, codex-sandboxing; fmt clean.
- Linux (glitch): see comment below.

issue.body:
Core integration fixtures on sync still assume upstream instruction placement, catalog overrides, sleep flags, subagent receipts, and writable-root rejection. Pin catalog-dependent scenarios per D644, scope deterministic nicknames to receipt snapshots, update eight dependent snapshots, and box session-construction futures in the three approvals tests so they fit the existing 8 MiB test stack. The macOS symlink test now verifies writes through both alias and real path while retaining an explicit read denial (#2143). No product code or product stack-size changes.

Related snapshot-only changes are merged as #2424/#2425. Failure grouping: #2296, [baseline detail](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/issues/2296#issuecomment-6918049177).

Validation on glitch, Rust 1.99.1, -j10, 8 MiB stack, eight test threads, isolated homes and 30-minute cap:
- Baseline lib: 4765 passed / 4 failed / 10 ignored. Lib code unchanged; not rerun after test-only changes.
- Baseline all: 2920 passed / 264 failed / 24 ignored; 24 CLI cases excluded (#2274); two hangs recorded separately.
- Baseline plus valid targeted reruns: **3015 passed / 169 failed / 24 ignored**, with the same excluded cases and baseline hangs. This is a combined result, not a fresh full-suite run: 95 fewer failures (five from correcting the runner FD limit, 90 from test/fixture/snapshot corrections), no newly failing case.
- Final corrective targeted run: 69 passed / 7 failed; the seven were four pre-existing first-party parameter-schema cases and three newly regenerated snapshots. All three snapshots were read, accepted, then passed a final 3/3 rerun. All three approvals edge cases passed at 8 MiB. A final preserved-fork filter run passed 3/3, resolving the last two baseline failures covered by that snapshot.
- Scoped clippy/fix completed successfully; its unrelated automatic product edits were removed before the test build. Changed Rust files pass Rust 1.99.1 rustfmt and git diff --check. Workspace formatting and CI are blocked by pre-existing CLI syntax errors.
- The macOS-only symlink test is not executed by Linux validation; native CI evidence remains subject to the sync CLI blocker.

Outstanding native parameter overrides, unexplained notification/history loss, timing/transport cases, shell-snapshot broker ownership (#2397), and additional missing-CLI cases are retained as failures, not masked. Independent read-only Opus 5.5 High review and corbanu-security exact-head approval are required before merge; all CI checks must complete and any red must be matched to sync base.

issue.title: Upstream Codex sync to rust-v0.165.0: scoping report

repository.name: CorbanuTerminal
repository.description: Corbanu Terminal: a capital-markets-focused AI coding and agent terminal.

issue.body:
This report measures what a fresh merge of upstream OpenAI Codex into `main` would take. It makes no decisions. The starting point is #94 by @goodalexander, who merged upstream `rust-v0.147.0` into the fork and wrote the upgrade record. That PR mapped the hotspots and the retained-behaviour checklist this sync needs, so thank you. #94 is being closed in favour of this sync (owner decision D219).

## Target and baseline

| | |
|---|---|
| Newest stable upstream release | `rust-v0.165.0` (published 2026-10-27), commit `360319d8dee62d87e2d59fc0c21805d79519cfed` |
| `main` measured at | `70281fe4e76d3a75ea52f406946b2224364d97b0` (2026-10-29) |
| Merge base (`main` ∩ 0.165.0) | `413492cd6c3a4d4f8dff6f406247ccda5a9d88aa` (2026-07-30), the same base #94 started from |
| Upstream commits since base | **3,807** (3,616 of them came after 0.147.0) |
| `main` commits since base | **6,731** |
| Upstream diff since base | 7,847 files, +1.19M / −208k lines |
| Toolchain | Rust 1.99.1 on both sides (no bump). `v8` goes 150.4.0 → **152.2.0** |

## Trial merge result

`git merge --no-commit --no-ff rust-v0.165.0` in a throwaway worktree on a local-only branch, aborted afterwards:

- **873 conflicted files**: 773 content, 62 modify/delete, 32 file-location (upstream directory moves), 6 add/add.
- **2,885 conflict hunks**, about **134k lines** inside conflict markers.
- 326 of the 873 are test files, including 135 insta snapshots. 38 are generated schemas or lockfiles that get regenerated, not hand-merged.
- For comparison: merging #94's target (0.147.0) into today's `main` gives 138 conflicts. On 2026-09-06 it gave 44. The gap grows quickly as both sides move.

### By area

| Area | Files | Hunks | Lines in conflict | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| tui | 259 | 621 | 33.5k | 20 modify/delete, 24 moved (`tui/src/analytics`) |
| core | 211 | 955 | 47.0k | 16 modify/delete (shell handlers, remote compaction) |
| other crates/tooling | 161 | 370 | 11.6k | state, ext, rollout, cli, mcp-server, core-skills, scripts |
| app-server | 56 | 195 | 8.3k | |
| config / providers / auth | 45 | 177 | 7.4k | model-provider(-info), models-manager, login |
| sandboxing (linux, network-proxy, shell-escalation) | 38 | 144 | 11.1k | `bwrap.rs` alone has 3.9k lines in conflict |
| config/schemas/locks | 38 | 241 | 7.7k | regenerate (`Cargo.lock`, `MODULE.bazel.lock`, schemas, `models.json`) |
| windows-sandbox | 20 | 61 | 3.3k | |
| CI/workflows | 16 | 44 | 1.0k | 4 workflows/actions deleted upstream |
| protocol (+ app-server-protocol src) | 15 | 40 | 1.8k | |
| exec / exec-server | 14 | 37 | 1.1k | |

### Heaviest hotspots

| File | Hunks | Lines | Corbanu features touched |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `core/src/session/mod.rs` | 60 | 2,458 | session wiring (security/provenance, accounting, agents) |
| `core/src/client.rs` | 45 | 2,315 | providers/catalog, permissions classifier hooks |
| `tui/src/app/tests.rs` | 18 | 9,067 | agents, vault, branding, classifier |
| `models-manager/models.json` | 37 | 4,423 | provider catalog, branding (regenerate + re-apply) |
| `linux-sandbox/src/bwrap.rs` | 23 | 3,865 | sandbox boundary |
| `tui/src/lib.rs` | 25 | 2,951 | branding/home dir, startup |
| `tui/src/app_server_session.rs` | 35 | 1,065 | session/agents |
| `core/src/session/turn.rs` | 34 | 723 | turn loop (classifier, agents) |
| `login/src/auth/manager.rs` | 27 | 971 | vault-backed credentials, providers |
| `network-proxy/src/credential_broker.rs` | 15 | 1,914 | credentials / sandbox network |
| `tui/src/model_catalog.rs` | 3 | 381 | provider catalog (346 Corbanu catalog lines on our side) |
| `core/src/agent/control.rs` + `control/mailbox.rs` | 18 | 1,454 | spawn / agent graph / mailbox |
| `tui/src/chatwidget/slash_dispatch.rs` | 7 | 352 | `/tasknode`, `/vault`, wallet/GPU slash commands |
| `core/src/exec_policy.rs` (+tests) | 8 | 772 | permissions classifier, vault, branding |

How often Corbanu identifiers show up on our side of the conflict hunks (approximate keyword match): branding/home dir 152 files, sandbox 119, spawn/agents 43 (agent-specific terms), providers/catalog 64, vault 39, permissions classifier 38, wallet/GPU/plan 29, Task Node 10. The classifier itself (`core/src/security/`) and the Corbanu-only crates (vault, tasknode-session, wallet, telegram) **do not conflict**. What conflicts is the upstream code that calls them.

### Structural upstream changes (these need porting, not just conflict resolution)

- **Shell tools moved onto unified exec** (upstream #39757). Upstream deleted `core/src/tools/handlers/shell.rs`, `runtimes/shell.rs` and `unix_escalation.rs`. `main` has 38 commits on those files. Our permission/sandbox behaviour there has to be re-hosted on the unified-exec path. **This is the main security risk.**
- **Patched zsh backend removed** (`shell-escalation` crate, #52160). **`codex mcp-server` removed** (#42993). **Legacy remote compaction removed** (#44273). `core-skills/src` split across several crates.
- **Repo guidance removed upstream** (`AGENTS.md`, `.codex/skills`, #49713). Keep ours.
- **24 new upstream crates**, some of which overlap with Corbanu features: `agent-roles`, `message-board`, `runtime-agent-instance` (vs our agent graph/mailbox), `mxc-sandbox`, `windows-sandbox-service`, `user-verification`, `workload-identity`, `guardian-context`.

## Effort and risk (rough)

- **Effort:** about 3–5 weeks of focused integrator work plus reviews, for one owner with agent help. Roughly 1–1.5 weeks for core + session, 1 week for tui, 1 week for sandbox/permissions porting and security review, and the rest for app-server/protocol/config, regeneration, CI and Windows.
- **Risk: high.** It changes the sandbox and permission surface (unified exec port, bwrap, windows sandbox, network-proxy credentials), so it needs security sign-off. The TUI conflicts are wide and snapshot-heavy. `main` is very active (about 70 commits/day since July), so a long-lived branch will drift. Each week of delay adds conflicts (0.147.0: 44 → 138 conflicts in 7 weeks).

## Suggested staging plan

1. **Freeze the target** at `rust-v0.165.0` and don't chase newer releases mid-sync. Keep one integration branch with a real two-parent merge, as #94 did.
2. **Mechanical pass:** take upstream for deleted/moved files where `main` didn't diverge meaningfully, keep our `AGENTS.md`/skills, regenerate lockfiles, `models.json` (then re-apply the Corbanu catalog), app-server and config schemas, and re-accept snapshots last.
3. **Per-area slices, one commit and one review each:** protocol/app-server-protocol → config/providers/auth (catalog, vault-backed login) → core (session, client, turn, agents/mailbox) → exec/unified-exec → tui (branding/home dir, catalog popups, slash commands, Task Node, `/spawn`) → app-server → other crates.
4. **Security slice (stops at "needs security sign-off"):** port the shell-handler permission/classifier/sandbox behaviour onto unified exec, plus bwrap, windows-sandbox, network-proxy `credential_broker` and `exec_policy`. Fail-before/pass-after tests for every boundary that moved.
5. **Qualification:** full CI including Windows clippy and native Windows tests, Linux full suite on glitch, cargo-deny, and true-TUI QA for providers, `/vault`, `/tasknode`, `/spawn`, wallet/GPU (no paid spend). Use #94's retained-behaviour checklist as the acceptance list.
6. **Afterwards:** smaller regular syncs (e.g. each upstream minor or monthly) so the gap doesn't grow back to thousands of commits.

## Recommendation (for Travis; not a decision)

Do the sync, targeting **`rust-v0.165.0`**. Start soon as a dedicated, owned program rather than in the background, because the conflict count grows weekly. If there isn't capacity for a 3–5 week program with a security review now, it's better to defer it explicitly and plan a regular cadence than to leave a half-done branch.

Measured by sync-scope94 on 2026-10-29. Raw data (conflict list, per-file hunks, merge log) is kept locally under `.codex-work/sync-scope94-data/`.

issue.title: CI: remaining PR test gaps after #1984 (dependents, macOS, test-support crates)

repository.name: CorbanuTerminal
repository.description: Corbanu Terminal: a capital-markets-focused AI coding and agent terminal.

issue.body:
Follow-up to #1972 / #1984. I'm filing this to record the repo-wide check and the gaps #1984 leaves.

## Before #1984

No Linux or macOS PR job ran any crate's `tests/*.rs`, apart from:
- the security suites in codex-core's `all` binary (`rust-ci-core-security.yml`)
- a few name-filtered `cargo test` runs in `corbanu-terminal-ci.yml`

The causes:
- **Linux Bazel tests** (`bazel.yml` `test`) run only with `cold_bazel`, which only nightly sets.
- **Windows gnullvm Bazel shards** skip without `BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY`.
- **The full Linux nextest suite** runs only postmerge.

On `main` (8d7b976c), 37 crates have `tests/*.rs`. The counts below are static counts of test attributes in `tests/**/*.rs`:

| crate | `tests/*.rs` files | tests |
|---|---|---|
| `codex-core` | 5 | 1467 |
| `codex-app-server` | 1 | 872 |
| `codex-exec-server` | 17 | 230 |
| `codex-cli` | 28 | 138 |
| `codex-exec` | 2 | 105 |
| `codex-tui` | 3 | 101 |
| `codex-linux-sandbox` | 1 | 81 |
| `codex-rmcp-client` | 17 | 76 |
| `codex-login` | 1 | 44 |
| `codex-otel` | 1 | 35 |
| `codex-state` | 4 | 33 |
| `codex-execpolicy-legacy` | 1 | 32 |
| `codex-execpolicy` | 1 | 27 |
| `codex-skills-extension` | 2 | 22 |
| `codex-goal-extension` | 2 | 22 |
| `codex-api` | 5 | 21 |
| `codex-network-proxy` | 2 | 18 |
| `codex-apply-patch` | 1 | 17 |
| `codex-secret-broker-fixture` | 3 | 15 |
| `codex-code-mode-host` | 2 | 13 |
| `codex-extension-api` | 3 | 11 |
| `codex-http-client` | 1 | 10 |
| `codex-mcp-extension` | 2 | 9 |
| `codex-core-skills` | 1 | 6 |
| `codex-mcp-server` | 1 | 5 |
| `codex-tools` | 1 | 2 |
| `codex-utils-rustls-provider` | 2 | 2 |
| `codex-chatgpt` | 1 | 2 |
| `codex-responses-api-proxy` | 1 | 2 |
| `codex-process-hardening` | 1 | 1 |
| `codex-agent-extension` | 1 | 1 |
| `codex-secret-broker-service` | 1 | 1 |
| `codex-security-audit` | 1 | 1 |
| `codex-cloud-tasks` | 1 | 1 |
| `codex-stdio-to-uds` | 1 | 1 |
| `codex-code-mode-runtime` | 1 | 1 |
| `codex-telegram` | 1 | 0 |
| **total** | | **3425** |

## After #1984

Every workspace crate's tests (unit and integration) run on Linux PRs that change a file under that crate. That covers all 37 crates above, with the helper binaries they need, so nothing in the list is left out.

| Trial (throwaway branch) | Job time |
|---|---|
| rmcp-client | 15 min |
| codex-core | 24 min |
| every crate at once | 46 min |

`CI required` already takes about 35 minutes.

## Remaining gaps

1. **Dependent crates.** A PR changing crate A doesn't run the tests of the crates that depend on A. For example, an rmcp-client change can break codex-core's MCP tests, and that shows up only postmerge. The same applies to a `Cargo.lock`-only change.
2. **macOS.** No CI lane, PR or postmerge or nightly, runs any crate's `tests/*.rs` on macOS, except codex-core's security suites.
3. **Test-support crates outside the workspace.** `core_test_support`, `app_test_support` and `mcp_test_support` are path dependencies, not workspace members, so their own unit tests (about 40) never run on PRs.
4. **Remote mode.** codex-core's remote-aware tests run only in local mode on PRs. Postmerge runs them with the Docker remote environment.

## Recommendation

- **(1) Dependent crates:** leave this to postmerge for now. Adding reverse dependencies would pull codex-core, tui and app-server into most PRs. If postmerge keeps catching such breaks, add reverse dependencies only for crates with a small fan-out (`cargo metadata` depth 1).
- **(2) macOS:** add a non-blocking macOS twin of `rust-ci-changed-crate-tests.yml` for a few crates with platform-specific code first (for example rmcp-client, exec-server and cli). Make it required only after it has a cost and flake record.
- **(3) Test-support crates:** add them to the workspace `members`, or select them explicitly in `changed_crate_test_packages.py`.
- **(4) Remote mode:** no action; postmerge covers it.
